history.content: What can you tell me about Formula One?

Formula One is the highest level of circuit racing defined by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), motor sports' world governing body. It can be seen live or tape delayed on television in almost every country and territory around the world. In the 2018 FIA Formula One World Championship, which is an ongoing motor racing championship, drivers and teams are competing in twenty-one Grands Prix for the World Drivers' and World Constructors' championship titles. The FIA also introduced tighter restrictions on racing licenses issued to drivers taking part in free practice sessions for the 2018 season. Candidate drivers are required to complete a minimum number of Formula 2 races or earn twenty-five superlicense points over a three-year period to address concerns about drivers who would not be able to meet the standards required to compete in Formula One having access to Formula One cars.
Where can I watch Formula One races?

The broadcasting rights for Formula One races vary depending on your location. On 14 October 2012, NBC Sports reached a 4 - year deal to broadcast Formula One races in the United States. The BBC continued to broadcast live coverage of half the races and all 20 races had ``extended highlights''. ESPN announced that it had acquired rights to Formula One under a multi-year deal beginning in 2018. ESPN had previously broadcast Formula One from 1984 to 1997.  ESPN Latin America broadcasts the highlights show on ESPN F1. The show highlights the races, from the practices to the checkered flag and shows interviews with the F1 drivers. Channel 4 's live broadcasts for 2016 were Bahrain, Spain, Europe, Britain, Hungary, Belgium, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico and Abu Dhabi.
How do I follow the Scottish Premier League?

The Scottish Premier League ( SPL ) was the top level league competition for professional football clubs in Scotland. Exclusive television rights for live Scottish Premier League matches were held by Sky Sports. BBC Scotland 's Sportscene held the rights to broadcast highlights of each match first on terrestrial TV. The BBC also held the rights to show online Internet highlights to UK users for one week after each match. The SPL was broadcast in Australia by Setanta Sports Australia, in Canada by Sportsnet World and in the United States by Fox Soccer Channel. Radio broadcasting rights were held by BBC Radio Scotland.
